strategyReview: Live one-touch NO selling continues to work (4/4 wins, avg +18.4%), weekend HL funding reversion long is solid across stocks (69% win, +1.40 aggregate), and PC ratio extremes show modest but consistent edge. The main failures are in shadow strategies: no-bias adjusted gap shadows lose heavily (–1.21 total), relative value heatmap shadows are large losers, PM proxy shorts (funding and PC ratio) on gold have <20% win rates, and cross-asset BTC momentum relying on HYPE confirmation delivers only 40% win. Several shadow-mined funding-reversion signals (CBRS, AAPL, MU) underperform when entered on a simple -10% threshold, and gold one-touch NO edges with large underlying-cap edge (≥10 pts) are 0% win in shadow tests.

failureClusters.evidence: FUNDING_EXTREME_LONG_PM_PROXY_SHORT on GOLD has 3/19 wins (16% win, avg PnL –2.67%); PC_RATIO_EXTREME_LOW_PM_PROXY_SHORT on GOLD 1/14 wins (7% win, avg PnL –4.99%). Both short GOLD via Polymarket when perp funding is extremely long or put/call ratio is extremely low, but the underlying spot often continues to rise or fails to decline meaningfully.
failureClusters.recommendation: Kill or completely redesign these proxy-short signals on gold. The correlation between extreme funding/call-buying and imminent spot declines is broken; the signals likely capture a sustained up-trend that traps shorts.

failureClusters.theme: No‑Bias Adjusted Gap Shadow — widespread losses
failureClusters.evidence: 93 resolved shadows, 39 wins (42% win), total PnL –1.21. The shadow buys no-bias-adjusted cheap NO side across assets. The high loss rate and large negative tails show the adjustment does not reliably identify mispricing.
failureClusters.recommendation: Retire the no-bias shadow strategy. The gap signal is not predictive; use the no-bias metric only as a supplement to other directional edges, not standalone.

failureClusters.theme: Large underlying‑cap edge on gold one‑touch NO is not a sell signal
failureClusters.evidence: H‑534 tested on GOLD with gold_pm_underlying_cap_edge_pts_max ≥10, predicting >2% spot decline. All 20 scorable tests lost, with gold moving sideways or higher. The edge does not mean the YES side is overpriced; it often reflects model miscalibration or genuine upside demand.
failureClusters.recommendation: Do not use large underlying‑cap edges alone to fade gold upside NO. If gold one‑touch edges are worth fading, use moderate edges (3‑8 pts) and near‑expiry contracts as in FIND‑0036.

failureClusters.theme: Cross‑asset BTC momentum with HYPE confirmation fails
failureClusters.evidence: The cross-asset family (H‑108, etc.) has 40% win across 15 tests despite promising initial clustered wins. HYPE spot above SMA and stable OI do not reliably confirm BTC follow‑through; the signal often fires when BTC is already extended.
failureClusters.recommendation: Simplify BTC momentum signals by removing HYPE conditions and relying only on BTC’s own trend and possibly vol regime.

newHypotheses.description: Fade moderate underlying‑cap edge on gold one‑touch NO with near‑expiry contracts. Restrict to upside barriers, edge between 3 and 8 points, and expiry ≤30 days to avoid the model‑miscalibration problem that kills large-edge signals.
newHypotheses.prediction: GOLD spot declines >2% within 2 days after the signal fires.

newHypotheses.description: CBRS funding reversion using regime‑relative extremity. Replace static < –10% with cbrs_hl_funding_ann in the bottom 5% of its trailing 7‑day distribution, capturing genuine panic overshoots instead of noisy negative periods.
newHypotheses.prediction: CBRS spot gains >2% within 2 days as funding normalizes from extreme negative outlier.

newHypotheses.description: AAPL funding reversion using regime‑relative extremity. Switch from < –10% to aapl_hl_funding_ann_percentile_7d < 5, isolating true tail events where funding is extremely negative relative to recent history.
newHypotheses.prediction: AAPL spot appreciates >2% within 2 days following an extreme negative funding tail.

newHypotheses.description: MU funding reversion with extreme tail filter. Use mu_hl_funding_ann_percentile_7d < 5 instead of absolute < –10%, so the signal only triggers on the most oversold funding prints.
newHypotheses.prediction: MU spot rises >2% within 2 days as deeply negative funding normalizes.

newHypotheses.description: BTC trend‑following without HYPE confirmation. Drop the HYPE overlap conditions; go long BTC when spot is above the 24h SMA and within 3% of the 7‑day high.
newHypotheses.prediction: BTC will deliver >2% spot gain over the next 7 days.

newHypotheses.description: BTC spot momentum without IV confirmation. Remove the rising options‑IV condition and keep pure momentum: spot above 24h SMA, near 7d high, and 24h gain >0.75%.

Short GOLD when put/call ratio falls into the bottom 10% of its 7‑day range (extreme call buying). The finding suggests this works even when the engine’s positive‑trend block would normally prevent the short.
BTC‑specific one‑touch NO edge: when a BTC upside one‑touch NO contract offers a sell‑YES edge of at least 3 points, short the YES side.
newHypotheses.prediction: BTC spot will not touch the high barrier, and the sold YES will expire worthless or the premium edge will contract, generating profit.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H‑534 tested the idea that a large underlying‑cap edge (≥10 pts) on gold upside one‑touch NO contracts predicts a >2% spot decline within 2 days. Every scorable test (20/20) lost; gold either moved sideways or rallied. The edge is not an actionable fade because the YES price often reflects genuine demand or model miscalibration, not overpricing.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A large underlying‑cap edge on gold upside one‑touch NO contracts reliably predicts a >2% spot decline within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H‑539 attempted to capture CBRS funding normalization from deeply negative levels (< –10%). Only 45% of tests won; funding often stayed negative or became more extreme before reverting. The simple threshold does not isolate true panic overshoots.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: CBRS funding below –10% reliably normalizes within 2 days and leads to a >2% spot gain.

hypothesisReviews.observation: AAPL funding reversion from < –10% produced 53% wins with large whipsaws. The signal fires too frequently during moderate negative regimes; the real edge, if any, is in extreme outliers.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: AAPL funding below –10% rapidly normalizes and yields a >2% spot gain.

hypothesisReviews.observation: MU funding below –10% led to mixed results (45% win). Like other single‑stock funding signals, the threshold lacks differentiation between routine dips and true excesses.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: Extreme negative MU funding (< –10%) rapidly normalizes and produces >2% spot gain.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H‑108 combined BTC momentum conditions with HYPE confirmation (spot above SMA, OI stable). Despite early wins, the overall win rate is 40%. HYPE participation does not reliably add predictive value; it often introduces false positives when BTC itself is already extended.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: HYPE spot above SMA with stable OI confirms a >2% BTC long move over 3–7 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H‑170 and related BTC listed‑IV momentum hypotheses required both spot momentum and rising options IV. With 27% win rate, the IV filter materially hurts performance. Rising IV often reflects hedging demand that coincides with, not predicts, further rally, and the signal triggers at exits rather than starts of moves.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: BTC spot momentum confirmed by rising options IV leads to further >2% gains within 3‑7 days.

journalEntry: Tonight we diagnosed six struggling setup families. Gold one‑touch NO with large underlying‑cap edge (H‑534) is a total failure — the edge is not a fade signal. Several shadow‑mined funding reversion signals (CBRS, AAPL, MU) are sub‑50% win under simple <-10% thresholds, so we proposed refinements using trailing 7‑day percentiles to isolate genuine tail events. Cross‑asset BTC momentum with HYPE confirmation (H‑108) and listed‑IV momentum (H‑218) are underperforming, so we created simpler variants stripping away the noisy overlays. From the ranked research findings, we authored two new hypotheses: a GOLD PC‑ratio extreme‑low short (FIND‑0053, 100% in‑sample shadow win) and a BTC‑specific one‑touch NO edge with ≥3 pt edge (FIND‑0043). No parameter changes tonight; risk levels remain appropriate.
